course.title: Hydrology and Water Resources Engineering
course.department: Department of Civil Engineering, CHRIST (Deemed to be University), Kengeri Campus

units.title: Introduction to Hydrology and Precipitation
units.syllabus: Definition and importance of hydrology; hydrologic cycle. Precipitation: forms and types; Symons' and syphon rain gauges; optimum number of rain-gauge stations; consistency (double mass curve); mean rainfall (arithmetic, Thiessen, isohyetal); missing data (arithmetic, normal ratio, regression); presentation (moving average, mass curve, hyetograph, IDF curves); Thiessen polygon map from meteorological data.

units.title: Components of Precipitation (Losses and Runoff)
units.syllabus: Evaporation (IS Class A pan, empirical formulae); infiltration (double-ring infiltrometer, Horton's equation, indices); runoff, catchment, water budget, rainfall-runoff regression; evapotranspiration (AET, PET, Penman, Blaney-Criddle); verification of losses with software; GIS rainfall-runoff model.

units.title: Hydrographs
units.syllabus: Hydrograph definition and components; unit hydrograph and its derivation from simple storm hydrographs; base-flow separation; S-curve and its uses.

units.title: Stream Flow Measurement and Flood Routing
units.syllabus: Measurement of stage; discharge by area-velocity and slope-area methods; stage-discharge relation; streamflow with software. Hydrological flood routing: reservoir and channel routing; flood frequency and forecasting; extreme events.

units.title: Ground Water Hydrology and Rainwater Harvesting
units.syllabus: Scope of groundwater hydrology; aquifer parameters; steady radial flow to wells in confined and unconfined aquifers; types of wells and construction. Rainwater harvesting: small-scale and small-tank, urban harvesting, groundwater recharge.

pages.title: Software setup

pages.title: Project (PBL)
pages.hook: One real catchment, four milestones, one driving question.

pages.title: Assessment
pages.hook: CIA components, AI-use log, data citation.

pages.title: References

software.title: About HEC-HMS
software.hook: The rainfall–runoff model at the centre of the course: what it is, how a model is organised, what happens in a subbasin.

software.title: About QGIS
software.hook: The GIS for gauges, polygons, DEMs and maps: vector vs raster, coordinate systems, the tools we use.

software.title: About HEC-RAS
software.hook: River hydraulics: water levels, velocities and flood extents from discharge.

software.title: About HEC-SSP
software.hook: Flood-frequency analysis (Bulletin 17C, log-Pearson III) with confidence limits.

labs.title: Install HEC-HMS and explore a working model
labs.goal: Install HEC-HMS, open the Castro Valley sample, run it, and map every component to the hydrologic cycle.

labs.title: Start the course project: basin model, subbasin and outlet
labs.goal: Create your own HEC-HMS project and draw the 54.85 km² teaching catchment as one subbasin draining to an outlet.

labs.title: Rain gauges in HEC-HMS: the Time-Series Data Manager
labs.goal: Enter the recording gauge TG1 (30-minute storm) and the three non-recording gauges TG2–TG4.

labs.title: First simulation: meteorologic model, control specs and results
labs.goal: Drive the subbasin with TG1, run the model and read the result graph and summary table.

labs.title: Gage Weights: Thiessen vs arithmetic mean in HEC-HMS
labs.goal: Type Thiessen and arithmetic weights into two meteorologic models and compare the runs.

labs.title: Missing data inside HEC-HMS
labs.goal: See what a blank cell does to a run, and run the model with a gap filled by the normal-ratio method.

labs.title: Hyetographs, cumulative curves and exporting results
labs.goal: Read hyetographs and mass curves from HEC-HMS, export time-series tables to a spreadsheet.

labs.title: A design storm: the Frequency Storm method
labs.goal: Turn IDF depths into 25- and 100-year design storms and compare their floods with the observed storm.

labs.title: QGIS: Thiessen polygons from station data
labs.goal: Load gauges and a catchment, build Voronoi polygons, clip, compute areas and weights, and print a map.

labs.title: HEC-HMS GIS: delineate a catchment from a DEM
labs.goal: Download and prepare a DEM, then let HEC-HMS fill sinks, find streams and delineate subbasins for your PBL site.

labs.title: HEC-HMS Loss Methods: Initial and Constant / Deficit and Constant
labs.goal: Configure and compare initial and constant loss parameters against a 24-hour design storm in HEC-HMS.

labs.title: HEC-HMS SCS Curve Number: Parameter Estimation and Subbasin Loss
labs.goal: Assign composite curve numbers and initial abstraction to subbasins in HEC-HMS and simulate excess runoff.

labs.title: HEC-HMS Evapotranspiration: Monthly Average and Gridded ET
labs.goal: Implement meteorological models with monthly evaporation rates and observe the effect on catchment water balance.

labs.title: Continuous Simulation: Soil Moisture Accounting (SMA) Model Setup
labs.goal: Configure the HEC-HMS 12-parameter Soil Moisture Accounting loss method across multi-month monsoon records.

labs.title: Model Calibration and Loss Parameter Verification with Observed Hydrographs
labs.goal: Calibrate loss rates and initial abstraction by minimizing error against observed streamflow gauge hydrographs.

labs.title: GIS-Based Rainfall-Runoff Modeling: Catchment Losses with QGIS and HEC-HMS
labs.goal: Derive spatially distributed land use and soil curve numbers in QGIS and export directly to an HEC-HMS basin model.

sessions.title: Hydrology, the hydrologic cycle and the water budget
sessions.hook: What hydrology is for, how water moves, and the one equation every model obeys.
sessions.lab: Water-budget problems by hand; install HEC-HMS and QGIS at home

sessions.title: Precipitation: forms, types and weather systems
sessions.hook: Rain, snow, hail; frontal, cyclonic, convective, orographic — and a first look inside HEC-HMS.
sessions.lab: Open the Castro Valley sample project, run it, and map each HMS component to the hydrologic cycle

sessions.title: Measuring rainfall and designing a rain-gauge network
sessions.hook: Symons', syphon (float), tipping-bucket and weighing gauges; how many gauges a catchment needs.
sessions.lab: Start the course model: create a project and enter a recording-gauge storm as a precipitation gage
sessions.keywords: rain gauge network optimum number Cv

sessions.title: Consistency of rainfall records: the double mass curve
sessions.hook: Spot a station whose record has drifted, and correct it.
sessions.lab: Build a double mass curve in a spreadsheet; load the corrected series into HMS

sessions.title: Mean areal rainfall: arithmetic, Thiessen and isohyetal
sessions.hook: Three ways to turn point rainfall into catchment rainfall — and why they disagree.
sessions.lab: Gage Weights meteorologic model in HEC-HMS: arithmetic vs Thiessen weights

sessions.title: Estimating missing rainfall data
sessions.hook: Arithmetic average, normal-ratio and regression methods for filling gaps.
sessions.lab: Fill a gap in a station record, then see what the gap does to HMS precipitation

sessions.title: Presenting rainfall data: mass curve, hyetograph, moving average
sessions.hook: Read a storm from its mass curve; smooth a 30-year record to see the trend.
sessions.lab: Hyetograph and cumulative-depth plots in HMS; moving average in a spreadsheet

sessions.title: Frequency analysis and intensity-duration-frequency curves
sessions.hook: Return period, probability and risk; building and using IDF curves.
sessions.lab: Frequency Storm meteorologic model in HMS driven by IDF depths
sessions.keywords: IDF return period risk weibull DAD

sessions.title: Thiessen polygon map in QGIS and catchment delineation
sessions.hook: From station coordinates and a DEM to polygons, weights and a basin outline. PBL launch.
sessions.lab: Voronoi polygons in QGIS; terrain-based subbasin delineation in HMS

sessions.title: Losses from precipitation; evaporation process and factors
sessions.hook: Where rainfall goes before it becomes runoff; what drives evaporation.
sessions.lab: Find every 'loss' slot in an HMS subbasin: canopy, surface, loss method, ET

sessions.title: Measuring and estimating evaporation
sessions.hook: IS Class A pan, pan coefficient, Meyer's formula and reservoir evaporation.
sessions.lab: Monthly Average evapotranspiration method in HMS from pan data

sessions.title: Infiltration: process, factors and the double-ring infiltrometer
sessions.hook: Infiltration capacity vs rate; reading an infiltrometer test.
sessions.lab: Plot infiltrometer data; Initial & Constant loss in HMS

sessions.title: Horton's equation and infiltration indices
sessions.hook: Fitting Horton's curve; φ-index and W-index from a storm.
sessions.lab: Compute φ-index by hand, then match it with the HMS constant-rate loss

sessions.title: Evapotranspiration: AET, PET and their measurement
sessions.hook: Lysimeters, field plots, and the difference between what could and what did evaporate.
sessions.lab: Hargreaves / Priestley-Taylor ET in an HMS continuous simulation

sessions.title: Penman's equation and the Blaney-Criddle formula
sessions.hook: Energy-balance and temperature-based PET; solved problems.
sessions.lab: Penman PET in a spreadsheet; compare with the HMS ET method

sessions.title: Runoff: catchment, components and factors affecting
sessions.hook: Surface, interflow and base flow; catchment characteristics that shape runoff.
sessions.lab: SCS Curve Number loss and catchment parameters in HMS

sessions.title: Rainfall-runoff relationship by simple regression
sessions.hook: Fit R = aP + b, judge the fit, use it for prediction.
sessions.lab: Run several storms through HMS and regress simulated runoff on rainfall

sessions.title: Verifying losses with software: a GIS rainfall-runoff model
sessions.hook: Close the loop: analytical losses vs the HMS model of your PBL catchment. PBL Milestone 2.
sessions.lab: Complete event model of the PBL catchment; compare with hand calculations

sessions.title: The hydrograph and its components
sessions.hook: Rising limb, crest, recession; time to peak, lag and time base.
sessions.lab: Read and annotate an HMS outflow hydrograph

sessions.title: Factors affecting the flood hydrograph
sessions.hook: Shape, size, slope, land use and storm movement.
sessions.lab: Sensitivity runs in HMS: area, CN, lag, storm duration

sessions.title: Base-flow separation
sessions.hook: Straight-line, fixed-base (N = 0.83 A^0.2) and variable-slope methods.
sessions.lab: Recession baseflow method in HMS vs hand separation

sessions.title: Effective rainfall hyetograph and direct runoff hydrograph
sessions.hook: ERH from φ-index; DRH volume equals effective rainfall volume.
sessions.lab: Excess precipitation and direct runoff from HMS result tables

sessions.title: The unit hydrograph: concept and assumptions
sessions.hook: Linearity, time invariance, and why one curve describes a catchment.
sessions.lab: User-Specified Unit Hydrograph transform in HMS

sessions.title: Deriving a unit hydrograph from a simple storm
sessions.hook: From observed flood to D-hour UH, step by step.
sessions.lab: Derive a UH in a spreadsheet; enter it in HMS and check the volume

sessions.title: Unit hydrograph for complex storms
sessions.hook: Superposition and convolution for multi-period effective rainfall.
sessions.lab: Convolution in a spreadsheet vs HMS for the same storm

sessions.title: The S-curve and its uses
sessions.hook: Summation hydrograph: construction and equilibrium discharge.
sessions.lab: Build an S-curve in a spreadsheet; check equilibrium discharge 2.778 A/D

sessions.title: Changing unit hydrograph duration; synthetic unit hydrographs
sessions.hook: D-hour to T-hour UH by S-curve; Snyder and SCS for ungauged catchments. PBL Milestone 3 begins.
sessions.lab: S-curve conversion; Snyder and SCS UH transforms in HMS

sessions.title: Streamflow measurement and measurement of stage
sessions.hook: Theory: Hydrometry & stage measurement (staff, wire, radar). Numericals: Staff gauge datum conversion & bubble gauge calibration. Lab: Install HEC-RAS & explore river geometry.
sessions.lab: HEC-RAS: Setup 1D river reach geometry and cross-section stations.

sessions.title: Discharge by the area-velocity method
sessions.hook: Theory: Area-velocity method, current meter rating v = a + bN. Numericals: Mid-section and mean-section method discharge computation. Lab: Enter surveyed river geometry into HEC-RAS.
sessions.lab: HEC-RAS: Cross-section input, Manning's n roughness assignment.

sessions.title: Discharge by the slope-area method
sessions.hook: Theory: Slope-area indirect discharge measurement, Manning's formula. Numericals: High-water mark reach slope & peak discharge calculation. Lab: Steady-flow simulation in HEC-RAS.
sessions.lab: HEC-RAS: Steady-flow analysis matching observed flood levels.

sessions.title: Stage-discharge relation (rating curve)
sessions.hook: Theory: Stage-discharge rating curve Q = Cr(G - a)^b, controls. Numericals: Log-log regression to determine rating curve parameters Cr and b. Lab: Define downstream rating curve boundary.
sessions.lab: HEC-RAS: Rating curve downstream boundary condition setup.

sessions.title: Flood routing: hydrologic and hydraulic
sessions.hook: Theory: Shifting controls, loop rating curves, backwater & unsteady flow. Numericals: Jones formula discharge correction for unsteady flood wave. Lab: Mixed flow regime modeling.
sessions.lab: HEC-RAS: Subcritical, supercritical, and mixed flow regime profiles.

sessions.title: Reservoir routing: Modified Puls method
sessions.hook: Theory: Dilution gauging, chemical tracers, ultrasonic & electromagnetic methods. Numericals: Constant-rate tracer injection mass balance equation. Lab: River calibration with tracer flow data.
sessions.lab: HEC-RAS: Compare 1D hydraulic profile with field-measured flows.

sessions.title: Channel routing: Muskingum method
sessions.hook: Theory: Flood frequency analysis, return period T, plotting positions (Weibull, Hazen). Numericals: Return period & exceedance probability calculation. Lab: Extract annual maximum series.
sessions.lab: HEC-SSP: Setup annual maximum flood series for frequency analysis.

sessions.title: Flood frequency (Gumbel) and flood forecasting
sessions.hook: Theory: Gumbel's extreme value Type I distribution, frequency factor K_T. Numericals: 50-year and 100-year peak design flood estimation by Gumbel's method. Lab: Gumbel fitting in HEC-SSP.
sessions.lab: HEC-SSP: Fit Gumbel distribution to observed annual peak flows.

sessions.title: Extreme events; reservoir sedimentation and sediment yield
sessions.hook: Theory: Log-Pearson Type III distribution, flood risk, safety margin. Numericals: Hydrologic risk and probability of at least one failure in n years. Lab: LP3 fitting and confidence limits.
sessions.lab: HEC-SSP: Fit Log-Pearson Type III distribution with 95% confidence bounds.

sessions.title: Groundwater: scope, occurrence and aquifer types
sessions.hook: Theory: Groundwater occurrence, vertical zones, aquifer types (confined, unconfined, leaky). Numericals: Porosity, specific yield, and specific retention. Lab: QGIS aquifer layer mapping.
sessions.lab: QGIS: Delineate regional hydrogeological units and recharge zones.

sessions.title: Aquifer parameters
sessions.hook: Theory: Darcy's law, range of validity, hydraulic conductivity K, intrinsic permeability. Numericals: Darcy flux, discharge velocity, and seepage velocity calculation. Lab: Hydraulic gradient map in QGIS.
sessions.lab: QGIS: Interpolate groundwater elevation contours from well observations.

sessions.title: Darcy's law and steady flow to a well in an unconfined aquifer
sessions.hook: Theory: Transmissibility T = Kb, storativity S, specific capacity of wells. Numericals: Transmissibility & storage coefficient estimation from aquifer test. Lab: Baseflow parameter estimation.
sessions.lab: HEC-HMS: Set linear reservoir baseflow parameters from hydrogeology.

sessions.title: Steady flow to a well in a confined aquifer
sessions.hook: Theory: Steady radial flow to well in unconfined aquifer (Dupuit-Thiem). Numericals: Well discharge and hydraulic conductivity from observation wells. Lab: Wellhead protection zone buffer.
sessions.lab: QGIS: Buffer calculation for wellhead sanitary protection zones.

sessions.title: Types of wells and methods of construction
sessions.hook: Theory: Steady radial flow to well in confined aquifer (Thiem equation). Numericals: Confined aquifer discharge and drawdown cone computation. Lab: Drawdown cone 3D surface.
sessions.lab: QGIS: Create raster surface of regional drawdown cone.

sessions.title: Rainwater harvesting: small-scale and small-tank systems
sessions.hook: Theory: Unsteady radial flow to confined well (Theis non-equilibrium equation). Numericals: Well function W(u) calculation and drawdown prediction. Lab: Aquifer test curve matching in Python.
sessions.lab: Python/QGIS: Type curve matching for Theis non-equilibrium equation.

sessions.title: Urban rooftop rainwater harvesting and storage sizing
sessions.hook: Theory: Cooper-Jacob straight-line approximation method, limits of validity (u < 0.01). Numericals: Graphical determination of T and S from semilog time-drawdown data. Lab: Automated Cooper-Jacob fitting.
sessions.lab: Python: Fit Cooper-Jacob straight-line regression to pump test data.

sessions.title: Methods of groundwater recharge
sessions.hook: Theory: Well losses, aquifer losses, well efficiency, recuperation test. Numericals: Specific capacity and recuperation constant computation for open well. Lab: Safe yield analysis.
sessions.lab: Spreadsheet/Python: Open well recuperation test analysis.

sessions.title: PBL showcase: catchment solutions
sessions.hook: Theory: Managed aquifer recharge (MAR), rainwater harvesting, groundwater quality. Numericals: Artificial recharge trench capacity & catchment recharge volume. Lab: Groundwater balance map.
sessions.lab: QGIS: Multi-criteria spatial decision analysis for recharge site suitability.
